close.note: All package, adversarial, real-workspace and independent QA gates pass; no Critical or Major findings remain.
close.summary: Made managed checkpoint path safety authoritative across discovery, Integrity, Doctor, canonicalization, retirement and close-sprint without restoring global blast radius.
recommendations: Decide the next patch version only when authorizing release; local metadata remains 4.47.1.
Continue maker/checker provenance and startup-contract consolidation as separate scopes.
learnings: Path identity and path safety are separate axes: registration or regular Kyro evidence determines ownership, while lstat-based inspection determines whether a managed path is consumable.
A durable initial lease permits a lease-relative worker startup budget, but protected work must still wait for the first completed renewal to avoid racing its atomic rename.

beforeClose.title: Managed checkpoint path safety
beforeClose.objective: Make checkpoint path safety authoritative across discovery and every consumer without reintroducing global blast radius.
successCriteria: Only regular checkpoints on fully safe managed paths are advertised as recoverable.
Registered or independently owned unsafe paths fail closed as owned-damaged in both Integrity and Doctor.
Unregistered unsafe entries without Kyro evidence remain FOREIGN and produce only a global Doctor warning.
No target reached through a symlink can influence discovery, blockers, commitments or resume.
Safe foreign registry contamination remains cleanable and apply diverges if its path becomes unsafe.

requirements.statement: Scope and checkpoint discovery must never dereference a symlink at the scope root, sprint, archive, record directory or checkpoint level.
requirements.rationale: An unsafe ancestor currently lets external names influence ownership and makes Integrity disagree with Doctor.

requirements.statement: Unsafe and unreadable managed paths must remain explicit internal facts rather than collapsing to absent or empty state.
requirements.rationale: Fail-open catch-to-empty behavior hides damage and produces false clean plans.

requirements.statement: An unregistered unsafe entry with no independent Kyro evidence must remain FOREIGN and only warn globally, while registered or evidenced unsafe state must be owned-damaged.
requirements.rationale: The registry and filesystem-evidence axes must protect owned state without restoring global blast radius.

requirements.statement: Integrity, Doctor, canonicalization, latest-checkpoint selection, retirement and close-sprint must consume one canonical checkpoint safety survey.
requirements.rationale: Parallel interpretations allowed Integrity to report clean while Doctor failed.

requirements.statement: No unsafe path may produce an integrity operation, before-commitment, canonicalization target or recovery promise.
requirements.rationale: Approval and replay must authenticate only executable safe inputs.

requirements.statement: Unregister-orphan must remain available for safe foreign contamination and must diverge if the directory becomes unsafe or gains Kyro evidence before apply.
requirements.rationale: Existing contaminated registries need cleanup without allowing a prepared plan to erase newly meaningful state.

requirements.statement: The existing blast-radius gate must prove the type, path and container guards are load-bearing through adversarial fixtures and mutation falsification.
requirements.rationale: A green suite that still passes after removing a safety guard does not certify that guard.

scenarios.given: a regular valid identity-matching checkpoint on a safe managed path and no sprint.json
scenarios.when: Integrity prepares and close-sprint retries
scenarios.then: Integrity reports recoverable-no-sprint and the real retry succeeds

scenarios.given: a checkpoint filename that is an internal, external, dangling or corrupt-target symlink
scenarios.when: discovery, Integrity and Doctor inspect it
scenarios.then: the link is never dereferenced, Integrity reports owned-damaged, Doctor fails and no operation is produced

scenarios.given: a directory named like a checkpoint file
scenarios.when: the canonical survey enumerates archive entries
scenarios.then: it is an unsafe non-regular candidate and never usable

scenarios.given: a registered valid scope whose root, sprint or archive path is symlinked
scenarios.when: Integrity and Doctor run
scenarios.then: both fail closed on the same unsafe path and Integrity never reports a clean plan

scenarios.given: an unregistered unsafe namespace entry with no independent regular Kyro evidence
scenarios.when: scope list, global Integrity and global Doctor run
scenarios.then: it is absent from scope list and Integrity and appears only as a Doctor warning

scenarios.given: an unsafe link whose target contents gain or lose Kyro-shaped names
scenarios.when: discovery runs before and after the target mutation
scenarios.then: classification, blockers and warnings remain identical

scenarios.given: a valid but unsafe unregistered scope
scenarios.when: install, sync and Integrity inspect it
scenarios.then: it is neither registered nor proposed for register-on-disk and no unsafe commitment is created

scenarios.given: a registered safe foreign directory from an older rehydrate
scenarios.when: unregister repair runs globally or scoped
scenarios.then: the registry entry is removed and the complete directory tree is unchanged

scenarios.given: a safe foreign unregister plan whose directory becomes unsafe or gains Kyro evidence
scenarios.when: apply executes the approved digest
scenarios.then: apply returns DIVERGED and neither project state nor the directory tree changes

scenarios.given: the type, path, container or catch-to-empty safety guard is independently removed in a temporary copy
scenarios.when: the blast-radius gate runs
scenarios.then: the corresponding adversarial assertion fails for the intended reason

nonGoals: Changing maker/checker provenance or approval identity.
Adding public commands, blocker codes or persistent schema states.
Touching NutriLens or another consumer repository.
Bumping version, installing, committing, pushing, releasing or publishing.

activeSprint.title: Authoritative managed path survey
activeSprint.objective: Establish one fail-closed managed-path survey and make every checkpoint consumer respect its registry-aware safety result.

phases.title: Safe discovery primitives
phases.objective: Represent path safety explicitly before any managed artifact is read or enumerated.

tasks.title: Harden managed path validation
tasks.description: Make assertSafeManagedPath detect dangling symlinks and reject symlinked or non-directory ancestors without following them.
tasks.context: existsSync treats a dangling symlink as absent, so the current component walk can skip it.
acceptance_criteria: Every existing path component is inspected with lstat semantics.
Dangling symlinks and non-directory intermediate components are rejected.
Lexical and real-path workspace escape protections remain intact.

evidence.summary: Hardened managed-path ancestry checks and stabilized lease-worker startup under filesystem load.

checked_criteria: Every existing path component is inspected with lstat semantics.

tasks.title: Make checkpoint survey authoritative
tasks.description: Extend the survey with container status, issue level and safe entry facts; never collapse unsafe or unreadable paths to an empty survey.
tasks.context: The current survey catches an unsafe archive ancestor and returns an empty list while ownership discovery performs a separate unsafe enumeration.
acceptance_criteria: Scope root, sprint, archive and checkpoint safety are observable without dereferencing links.
Only safe regular candidates reach checkpoint resolution.
Ownership scanning never enumerates an unsafe archive or record directory.
The five directory classes remain unchanged and path issues remain a separate axis.

phases.title: Registry-aware consumer parity
phases.objective: Apply the same safety facts to classification, repair, Doctor and checkpoint consumers.

tasks.title: Apply the registry and evidence matrix
tasks.description: Keep unregistered unsafe entries without Kyro evidence foreign and advisory, while treating registered or evidenced unsafe state as owned-damaged; protect rehydrate and unregister.
tasks.context: A registered unsafe directory is owned state, but an arbitrary unregistered symlink must not become a global blocker.
acceptance_criteria: Foreign unsafe entries are never registered and warn only globally.
Registered unsafe entries are owned-damaged and never unregister targets.
Safe foreign contamination remains cleanable.
Apply diverges if a prepared foreign directory becomes unsafe or owned.

evidence.summary: Applied the registry-by-evidence matrix to reconciliation, rehydration, resolution and unregister apply.

tasks.title: Unify Integrity and Doctor
tasks.description: Render the survey's issues consistently and exclude every unsafe path from operations, commitments, canonicalization, latest-checkpoint selection, retirement and resume.
tasks.context: A valid registered scope with a symlinked archive currently produces a clean Integrity plan and a failing Doctor result.
acceptance_criteria: Integrity and Doctor identify the same unsafe managed path.
Unsafe paths create no operations or before-commitments.
Only safeFiles feed latest-checkpoint, canonicalization and resume.
Duplicate findings for one issue are suppressed.

phases.title: Adversarial certification
phases.objective: Prove isolation, no-dereference, cleanup compatibility and load-bearing guards.

tasks.title: Extend the blast-radius matrix
tasks.description: Add portable root, sprint, archive, record and checkpoint path fixtures plus target-mutation and prepare/apply divergence coverage to the existing gate.
tasks.context: The current gate covers direct checkpoint links but does not make the candidate type or ancestor-path guard independently load-bearing.

Target contents behind a symlink cannot change results.
